propositions: The undeclared-paths gate's error message instructs authors to declare new paths and retry, but declaring them changes the material basis hash which causes a stale-material refusal on retry.

The close gate promises a bare retry after running `rebar set-file-impact` but the follow-up attestation gate blocks it as stale-material, creating an apparent contradiction that is actually two correct gates detecting one real condition.

Widening file_impact retroactively broadens what an existing attestation signature claims to cover, since the attestation scope is built from declared file_impact union cited files, so this is a material plan change requiring re-review.

The undeclared-paths error message must state that declaring new paths is a material change invalidating attestation and that `rebar review-plan` must be re-run before close can succeed, instead of implying a bare retry suffices.

No behavioural change to either gate is in scope; both gates must continue firing under exactly their current conditions; only the first message's wording requires clarification to document the re-attestation requirement.
